correctness.rationale: For all finite irreducible birth–death generators, adjacent differences intertwine Q and the irreducible negative-stable tridiagonal Metzler H. Rational calculus gives D T_h=(2R_h−I)D, and surjectivity of D makes increasing-cone preservation exactly entrywise nonnegativity of this edge map. For h>0 all off-diagonal edge resolvent entries are strictly positive by the Metzler integral representation. H is diagonally symmetrizable with strictly negative eigenvalues inherited from Q modulo constants, so each diagonal resolvent is a strictly decreasing sum of positive spectral weights, from one to zero. Every edge has exactly one half-crossing, and their minimum gives an if-and-only-if cutoff. Direct 2×2 inversion gives the general three-state formula. All rational examples and the four-state generator identity were checked with the embedded exact-arithmetic program.

originality.rationale: The continuous-time birth–death gradient/Feynman–Kac intertwining, stochastic monotonicity definitions, generic SSP monotonicity theory, and Crank–Nicolson entry-positivity resolvent criterion are explicitly treated as prior work. The claim is narrower and distinct: a sharp discrete Crank–Nicolson monotonicity cutoff on the increasing-function cone controlled by the killed edge resolvent, the complete three-rate closed form, and both directions of separation between entry positivity and stochastic order. The closest full primary papers inspected or searched do not give these coupled sharp statements. The calculation is natural but does not follow from the prior probability-positivity test by reinterpreting the original generator Q: the edge matrix is different, and the two constraints genuinely separate.
residual_risks: Chafaï–Joulin gives the exact continuous gradient intertwining; a numerical-analysis paper may already have applied it to the Crank–Nicolson rational map under dual-chain terminology.
The sharp order-resolvent cutoff is an algebraic consequence of the known killed-edge semigroup framework; prior literature might express it without the term stochastic order.
Only selected sections, not the central theorem pages, were inspected in Higueras 2006; the theoretical overlap comparison retains that access/read limitation.

Published stochastic monotonicity is sometimes defined only for genuine Markov matrices, so the standalone cone-preservation property must not be confused with stochastic monotonicity when entrywise positivity fails.

value.rationale: Stochastic-order preservation is needed for monotone coupling, comparison principles, and order-sensitive observables, whereas mass preservation and probability nonnegativity are separate basic requirements for a numerical transition step. The theorem gives a necessary-and-sufficient, computable per-edge spectral-resolvent step bound for any finite birth–death chain, plus a closed-form three-state phase diagram. Two exact three-state rate choices show that a perfectly valid nonnegative CN Markov transition can violate stochastic ordering while an order-preserving CN map can have negative transition entries. These opposite separations motivate checking both cones rather than relying on SSP bounds or probability-positivity tests alone.
